flagship.title: A small loop among the longleaf pines
flagship.standfirst: One easy mile at Weymouth Woods: tall longleaf pines, sandy ground and a generous pace, with a shorter loop beside the parking if that is enough for Rupert.
flagship.why_this_week: After Tuesday’s longer oak-hickory and wetland circuit, this is a different scale and landscape: one unhurried mile through the open longleaf pines of the main tract. Follow the blue-triangle Pine Barrens loop from visitor-center parking. Wildlife sightings are a possibility, not a promise. Allow an hour to an hour and a half for the walk and Rupert’s pauses. The western Equestrian Trail closure is separate from this route; do not extend onto that trail or assume the Boyd and Paint Hill tracts share this access. The publication-day NWS forecast is sunny and cool, with a northeast breeze on Saturday.

access.name: Visitor-center parking, 1024 Fort Bragg Road, Southern Pines
access.parking: Use the visitor-center lot on the main tract; the official map marks parking, restrooms and the Pine Barrens trail start. No day-use entry fee. October park hours 8 a.m.–8 p.m.; visitor center 8 a.m.–5 p.m. Rupert must stay outside the building.

dog.leash: Attended leash no longer than 6 feet; pets stay outside buildings.
dog.water: Carry drinking water and a bowl; no dog swimming is part of this outing.
dog.shade: An open longleaf-pine landscape rather than continuous deep shade; carry water even in cool weather.
watch_for: Dry sand, roots and pine litter underfoot
Give wildlife and protected habitat plenty of space

panels.label: A short main-tract loop
panels.text: The official Pine Barrens Trail is one mile, easy, and marked with blue triangles. Begin at visitor-center parking; the separate tracts are not part of this plan.

panels.label: Keep the closure separate
panels.text: The western Equestrian Trail has a maintenance closure. The suggested hiking loop does not use that segment; obey all on-site signs and recheck the status before leaving.

artwork.brief: One Rupert walking directly toward the viewer with his head lowered attentively and one forepaw lifted; full anatomically coherent body and slim tapered tail on a spare burgundy field. This differs from the recent olive standing profile, cream resting portrait and ochre ball-carrying close-up in action, frontal depth, full-body scale, negative space and dominant colour.

local_trail.title: A smaller circuit beside the lot
local_trail.line: Use the official 0.3-mile Bower’s Bog loop, marked with red circles, instead of the longer walk. Stay on the marked path and stop if the footing is unsuitable.

pivot.if: Thunder, strong wind, flooding, unsafe footing or an official closure
pivot.note: Postpone rather than substituting another exposed outing. Recheck official access and the current NWS forecast before leaving.

conditions.trail_note: Stay with the blue-triangle Pine Barrens loop. Avoid the closed western Equestrian Trail, carry water through the open pine landscape and turn back for unsafe footing or weather.

practical.best_window: Saturday morning after the cool start, or Sunday morning, in full daylight; expect a northeast breeze and finish well before the 8 p.m. gate.
practical.fees: No day-use entrance fee; reservations and special permits are separate.
bring: Attended six-foot leash and waste bags
A small picnic if the weather allows
practical.closures_note: Official NC State Parks home/status, trail table, news, access map and pet rules read on 22 October. Hiking Trails explicitly Open. The western Equestrian Trail segment along Bethesda Road remains closed for maintenance; the suggested one-mile Pine Barrens blue-triangle loop starts at main-tract visitor-center parking and does not use that segment. Main tract public address and GPS 35.1470,-79.3716 verified; October hours 8 a.m.–8 p.m., visitor center 8 a.m.–5 p.m.; free day use; pets on attended leashes no longer than six feet and outside buildings. The current NWS forecast supplies Saturday and Sunday daytime periods and returned no active alerts; absence of an alert is not a safety guarantee.
